description: The names the screen gives the player's choices and actions, and stance questions with their answers: short imperatives and questions American speakers say, mined from public-domain federal records (hearings, the Congressional Record, federal oral histories), with record words as slots. Each part names the core action id it labels.

slots.employer: An employer, from the job record.
slots.name: A person, by name, from the records.
slots.relation: A relative named by relation (your mother), from the family record.
slots.group: An organization, from the group record.
slots.place: A place, from the place or venue record.
slots.office: An office or officeholder, from the office records.
slots.cause: What the person's cause is about, from their drive record.
slots.topic: A stance topic as words, from the topic's record.
slots.change: The change a stance wants, as a verb phrase from the record.

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 2 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.
